mn31:1.2: One one occasion the Blessed One was living at Nādika in the Giñjaka House.
mn31:2.1: Now on that occasion the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Nandiya and the venerable Kimbila were living at the Park of the Gosinga (Cow’s Horn) Sāla-tree Wood.
mn31:3.1: When it was evening the Blessed One rose from meditation and went to the Park of the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.
mn31:3.2: The park-keeper saw the Blessed One coming.
mn31:3.4: ‘Do not come into this park, monk.
mn31:3.5: There are three clansmen here seeking their own good.
mn31:4.1: The venerable Anuruddha heard the park-keeper speaking to the Blessed One.
mn31:4.3: ‘Friend park-keeper, do not keep the Blessed One out.
mn31:4.4: It is our Master, the Blessed One, who has come.’
mn31:4.5: The venerable Anuruddha went to the venerable Nandiya and the venerable Kimbila and said:
mn31:4.6: ‘Come out, venerable sirs, come out: our Master has come.’
mn31:5.1: Then all three went to meet the Blessed One.
mn31:5.2: One took his bowl and outer robe, one prepared a seat, and one placed water for washing the feet.
mn31:5.3: The Blessed One sat down on the seat prepared,
mn31:5.4: and having done so, he washed his feet.
mn31:5.5: Then they paid homage to him and sat down at one side.
mn31:5.6: When they had done so, the Blessed One said to them:
mn31:5.7: ‘I hope that you are all keeping well, Anuruddha, that you all are comfortable, and that you have no trouble on account of alms-food.’
mn31:5.8: ‘We are keeping well, Blessed One, we are comfortable, and we have no trouble on account of alms-food.’
mn31:6.1: ‘I hope that you all live in concord and agreement, Anuruddha, as undisputing as milk with water, viewing each other with kindly eyes.’
mn31:6.3: ‘But, Anuruddha, how do you live thus?’
mn31:7.1: ‘Venerable sir, as to that, I think thus:
mn31:7.2: “It is gain for me, it is great gain for me
mn31:7.3: that I am living with such companions in the life divine.”
mn31:7.4: I maintain bodily, verbal and mental acts of living-kindness towards these venerable ones in public and in private.
mn31:7.8: “Why should I not set aside what I am minded to do and do only what they are minded to do?”
mn31:7.10: We are different in body, venerable sir, but only one in mind, I think.’
mn31:7.11: The venerable Nandiya and the venerable Kimbila each spoke likewise. They added:
mn31:7.23: ‘That is how we live in concord, venerable sir, as friendly and undisputing as milk with water, viewing each other with kindly eyes.’
mn31:8.2: I hope that you all dwell diligent, ardent and self-controlled.’
mn31:9.2: ‘But, Anuruddha, how do you dwell thus?’
mn31:9.3: ‘Venerable sir, as to that, whichever of us returns first from the village with alms-food prepares the seats, sets outs the water [for drinking and for washing and puts the refuse bucket in its place.
mn31:9.4: Whichever of us returns last eats any food left over, if he wishes; otherwise he throws it away where there is no greenery or drops it into water where there is no life.
mn31:9.5: He puts away the seats and the water for drinking and for washing. He puts away the refuse bucket after washing it, and he sweeps out the refectory.
mn31:9.6: Whoever notices that the pots of drinking water or washing water or water for the privy are low or empty sees to them.
mn31:9.7: If they are too heavy for him, he calls someone else by a sign of the hand and they move it by joining hands. We do not speak for that purpose.
mn31:9.8: But every five days we sit out the night together in talk on the Dhamma.
mn31:9.9: That is how we dwell diligent, ardent and self-controlled.’
mn31:10.2: but while dwelling diligent, ardent and self-controlled in this way, have you attained as a comfortable abiding any distinction worthy of a Noble One’s knowledge and vision, higher than the human dhamma?’
mn31:10.4: Here whenever we want, quite secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unprofitable dhammas, we enter upon and abide in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and sustained application, with happiness and pleasure born of seclusion.
mn31:10.5: Venerable sir, this is a distinction worthy of a Noble One’s knowledge and vision, higher than the human dhamma, which we have attained as a comfortable abiding while dwelling diligent, ardent and self-controlled.’
mn31:11-13.2: But is there any other distinction worthy of a Noble One’s knowledge and vision, higher than the human dhamma, which you have attained as a comfortable abiding by surmounting that abiding, by tranquillizing that abiding?’
mn31:11-13.4: Here whenever we want, with the stilling of initial application … the second jhāna … self-controlled.’
mn31:14.4: Here whenever we want, with the fading as well of happiness … the third jhāna … self-controlled.’
mn31:15.4: Here whenever we want, with the abandoning of (bodily) pleasure and pain … the fourth jhāna … self-controlled.’
mn31:16.4: Here whenever we want, with the complete surmounting of perceptions of form … base consisting of infinite space …’
mn31:18.2: But is there any other distinction worthy of a Noble One’s knowledge and vision, higher than the human dhamma, which you have attained as a comfortable abiding by surmounting that abiding, by tranquillizing that abiding?’
mn31:18.4: Here whenever we want, by completely surmounting the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception we enter upon and abide in the cessation of perception and feeling. And our taints are exhausted by our seeing with understanding.
mn31:18.5: Venerable sir, that is a distinction worthy of a Noble One’s knowledge and vision, higher than the human dhamma, which we have attained as a comfortable abiding by surmounting that (former) abiding, by tranquillizing that (former) abiding.’
mn31:18.8: There is no comfortable abiding higher or more sublime than that.’
mn31:19.1: Then when the Blessed One had instructed, urged, roused and encouraged the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Nandiya and the venerable Kimbila with a talk on the Dhamma, he rose from his seat and departed.
mn31:20.1: Now when they had accompanied the Blessed One a little on his way and turned back again, the venerable Nandiya asked the venerable Anuruddha and the venerable Kimbila:
mn31:20.2: ‘Have we ever announced to the venerable Anuruddha
mn31:20.3: our obtaining such and such abidings and attainments that he proclaims them in the Blessed One’s presence up to the exhaustion of taints?’
mn31:20.4: ‘The venerable ones have never announced to me
mn31:20.5: their obtaining of such and such abidings and attainments. Yet by encompassing the venerable ones’ minds with my mind it is known to me
mn31:20.6: that they have obtained such and such abidings and attainments.
mn31:20.7: Besides deities have told me this fact (saying:)
mn31:20.8: “These venerable ones have obtained such and such abidings and attainments.”
mn31:20.9: Then I declared it when directly questioned by the Blessed One.’
mn31:21.1: Then the spirit Digha the Sorcerer went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he stood at one side. When he had done so, he said:
mn31:21.2: ‘It is gain for the Vajjians, venerable sir, it is great gain for the Vajjians,
mn31:21.3: where the Tathāgata dwells, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, and these three clansmen,
mn31:21.4: the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Nandiya and the venerable Kimbila!’
mn31:21.5: And on hearing the voice of the spirit Digha the Sorcerer, the Earth gods responded:
mn31:21.9: And on hearing the voice of the Earth gods, the gods of the Four Kings responded: ‘It is gain …
mn31:21.11: … The gods who have Gone to Bliss …
mn31:21.13: … The gods who delight in Creating …
mn31:21.14: And on hearing the voice of the gods who delight in Creating, the gods who wield Power over Others’ Creations responded: ‘It is gain …’
mn31:21.15: And on hearing the voice of the gods who wield Power over Others’ Creations, the gods of the Retinue of the Divinity (Brahmā) responded:
mn31:21.16: ‘It is gain for the Vajjians, it is great gain for the Vajjians,
mn31:21.17: where the Tathāgata dwells, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, and these three clansmen,
mn31:21.18: the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Nandiya and the venerable Kimbila!’
mn31:22.1: ‘So it is, Digha, so it is.
mn31:22.2: And if the clan from which those three clansmen went forth from the home life into homelessness should remember them with confident heart, that would be long for the welfare and happiness of that clan.
mn31:22.3: And if the retainers of the clan from which those three clansmen went forth …
mn31:22.7: And if the country from which those three clansmen went forth from the home life into homelessness should remember them with confident heart, that would be long for the welfare and happiness of that country.
mn31:22.8: If all of the warrior-noble caste …
mn31:22.11: If all the artisan caste should remember them with confident heart, that would be long for the welfare and happiness of the artisan caste.
mn31:22.12: If the world with its gods, its Māras and its divinity (Brahmā), this generation with its monks and divines, with its kings and its men, should remember them with confident heart, that would be long for the welfare and happiness of the world.
mn31:22.13: See, Digha, how far these three clansmen are practising the way of welfare and happiness of the many out of pity for the world, for the benefit, welfare and happiness of gods and men!’
mn31:22.14: That is what the Blessed One said.
mn31:22.15: The spirit Digha the Sorcerer was satisfied, and he delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
